column1: # The red run: this tree's assertions against the engine the base ref holds,
# written whole by tests/red, which tests/run --record-assertions calls.
#   base  <ref>  <sha>  <engine version there>
#   run   <failed>  <passed>  <skipped>        lines counted, not the summary
#   <assertion name>  <times it failed>        failed names only
#   an assertion the manifest lists that the base run never reached counts as failed, by its shortfall
# A base of - means no complete red run was made: none was possible, the
# suite stopped before reached or reached no assertion, or tests/red itself
# was stopped; its stdout said which unless it was the one stopped.
# Reproduce with: tests/red <ref>
base
run
a GitHub Enterprise-shaped host is held too, since github.com's owner/name would not check it
a GitHub origin with no owner/name in it holds both rows, saying so
a failing gate heals the split row too, and its own row follows: two lines, the healed one first
a failing gate on an unborn HEAD still writes one row: today, main, unborn, the checks, the second and no session, byte for byte
a full felix commission adopts what the checkout shows before it runs: capabilities holds ci
a full felix commission heals the split row
a handoff written on an unborn HEAD names the branch it is on
a heal clears the leftovers of one killed part way, once they are over a minute old
a heal keeps the log's mode: a 600 log is healed and is still 600
a heal raced by an unlocked append keeps its own rows first: the joined pair, then the row that was there
a healed file gated again is left alone: the same bytes and the same mtime
a healed pair is one line
a live owner's lock stops the heal: the split file is left as it was
a lock whose owner has exited is taken over, and the pair joined
a lock with no pid, over a minute old, is taken over: the file is healed and the lock gone
a long legacy runbook with an empty slug begins with the preface, then shows --repo {{REPO}}, never --repo and a blank
a mixed file of seven lines holding two pairs heals to five
a non-GitHub remote leaves both slug rows waiting for a GitHub remote
a project FAIL line with no final newline is not swallowed by the engine line after it
a project gate that fails silently is recorded beside the probe that failed with it: exit-1, then probes
a remote carrying shell text is no slug: risk-labels is a step Felix says it cannot check
a remote whose host would be an ssh option is no GitHub remote: both rows wait
a row saved with an empty slug reads as waiting for a GitHub remote, like a {{REPO}} row
a runbook of 200 KB or more with {{REPO}} still begins with the no-remote preface
a session start heals a split row
a split row dated today is healed
an alias named for GitHub without github.com in it is held the same way
an ssh alias ssh cannot resolve holds both slug rows as todo, saying why, rather than letting them wait
and a healed pair has four tab-separated fields
and each pair is joined exactly once
and each pair is joined where it stood: lines 2 and 4
and felix log does too, a dash for no session and the branch of a checkout with no commit
and felix setup risk-labels begins by saying why {{REPO}} is left as written
and felix setup risk-labels prints the same runbook
and felix setup's screen is the same, apart from the project's name
and gh is asked nothing for it
and gh is asked nothing for the rows that wait
and gh is asked nothing for them, because no slug was read
and gh is asked the same questions
and gh was asked about acme/widget for both
and gh was asked about acme/widget for it
and its newest entry says the commit was unborn
and its runbook begins by saying {{REPO}} is left as written until origin points at GitHub
and its runbook shows --repo acme/widget in both places
and its well-formed rows keep their bytes and their places: lines 1, 3 and 5
and names the branch an unborn repository is on
and no mistakes row is written for a gate that never ran
and passes a well-formed file through byte for byte
and prints nothing for a missing file, returning 0
and procedures still name it through the link
and says it could not run, naming 126
and says it once, as the gate's last line, after the obligations line it depends on
and says its head is unborn rather than guessing one
and says the commit is unborn rather than guessing one
and setup.tsv gains ci's two slug rows with {{REPO}} kept
and shows --repo {{REPO}} in both places the empty slug was
and ssh is asked only for its configuration, with no DNS lookup, about the alias as written
and still says the gate command could not run
and the Stop hook's guard still names it through the link
and the commissioning policy version does not move
and the gate says it could not run, so nothing was tested and it is not recorded as failing
and the heal keeps the log's mtime
and the heal that took it over leaves no lock behind
and the pair becomes one row, byte for byte: the date, HEAD, unborn, and the checks with their trailing space
and the raced heal leaves no temporary, link or lock behind
and the recurrence report still reads the failure through the link
and the report says so, naming ci with what it added
and the row appended mid-heal survives exactly once, as the last of three lines
and the rust toolchain step names stable itself, since a commit carries no channel
and the same saved rows now read done, three fields, with the slug filled in
and the saved risk-labels runbook keeps {{REPO}} too
and two heals at once leave no temporary or lock behind
and with a gitlab remote gh is never called for them
and with its own status: exit-3, then probes
and with only a gitlab remote under another name, they wait
and writes no mistakes row for it either
as is the devlog entry, its header one line on a checkout with no commit
beside a failing probe, the line never says the run was not recorded, since probes was
but leaves a temporary younger than a minute to whoever owns it
every checkout in the generated workflow is v5, the lowest major on Node 24
every uses: in the gate workflow bootstrap renders names a full commit sha, for every stack it can render
every uses: in the unattended template names a full commit sha, not a ref its owner can move
felix new with no remote saves both slug rows with --repo {{REPO}}, never an empty slug
felix setup risk-labels prints the runbook with the slug filled in
felix setup shows risk-labels as a step to do, with the reason Felix cannot check it
felix setup shows risk-labels waiting for a GitHub remote, never as a step to do
felix_mem_mistake_rows, with resolve.sh alone, reads a split pair as its one joined row and leaves the file as it was
it says the command's own status is not recorded, and names the engine check that is
no engine file appends a fallback to what git said about HEAD
origin behind an ssh alias that ssh -G says stands for github.com gives acme/widget, so both read done
origin over ssh on port 443 gives acme/widget, not 443/acme/widget, so both read done
origin spelled with a trailing slash gives acme/widget, so both slug rows read done
procedures name the failure an unhealed split row holds
so gate_shown_failing is not satisfied by a gate that never ran

so gate_shown_failing sees the project's own silent failure there

so nothing is left undeclared after the run

so the receipt the run wrote is not stale at the next read
the Stop hook's guard names what an unhealed split row caught last
the monitor counts an unhealed split row once: three rows, not five
the next session start has nothing left to adopt
the recurrence report counts an unhealed split row: two occasions, unborn and a sha, over three runs
two failing gates at once over two split pairs leave four lines, the healed pairs of four fields and the gates' own rows of six
while the one real pair among them is joined in place, one line shorter
with a GitHub remote, a {{REPO}} row's status is byte for byte a baked row's
